text:
Colorado lost Nathan MacKinnon for what NHL.com reported as 12 weeks, and the first week without him went about as well as it could. The Avalanche have won three straight, outscoring teams 14-3, including a 6-0 shutout of Montreal and Friday's comeback in Minnesota, where they trailed 3-0 late in the third and won in a shootout on Cale Makar's goal. Michael Russo's Athletic piece on it carried the Wild's own verdict: "Don't know what happened."

The bigger question is what this team is without its best player for a quarter of the season. Before the injury it was one of the league's best: 15-7-3, 55% of the expected goals, and goals at both ends close to what the chances said once you allow for elite finishing (about 13 goals above expected, which for this roster is mostly skill). MacKinnon's line with Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas had outscored opponents 20-10.

Now the load moves to Makar, who had three assists in his return, and to Devon Toews (9 points in his last 10) beside him; that pair takes 60% of the expected goals. Brock Nelson steps onto the top line, and Gabriel Landeskog is producing on the power play.

Our numbers still give Colorado a 97% chance at the playoffs and a one in three shot at the division. What we'd watch: the five-on-five share over the next month, because the depth lines were the question before MacKinnon got hurt and they are the whole question now.
